'''Fernando Carlos Redondo Neri''' ({{IPA|es|feɾˈnando reˈðondo}}; born 6 June 1969) is an Argentine former professional [[association football|footballer]] who played as a [[Midfielder#Defensive midfielder|defensive midfielder]]. He most notably played for [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] and [[AC Milan]]. He is widely regarded as one of the greatest defensive midfielders of all time.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://iconicfootball.weebly.com/top-50-defensive-midfielders-of-all-time.html|title=Top 50 Defensive Midfielders of All-Time|website=Iconicfootball.weebly.com|access-date=9 July 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.sportbible.com/football/news-legends-revealed-110-nominees-for-france-footballs-ballon-dor-dream-team-20201022 | title=Full List of 110 Nominees for France Football's 'Ballon d'Or Dream Team' Have Been Revealed | date=22 October 2020 | access-date=26 June 2023 | archive-date=3 November 2020 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201103131208/https://www.sportbible.com/football/news-legends-revealed-110-nominees-for-france-footballs-ballon-dor-dream-team-20201022 | url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-07-28 |title=Best defensive midfielders ever |url=https://www.fourfourtwo.com/features/best-defensive-midfielders-ever |access-date=2024-10-12 |website=FourFourTwo |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Churchill |first=Max |date=2025-01-18 |title=The 10 greatest defensive midfielders in football history ranked - Rodri 8th |url=https://www.givemesport.com/greatest-defensive-midfielders-in-football-history-ranked/ |access-date=2025-09-30 |website=GiveMeSport |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/949512-50-best-defensive-midfielders-in-world-football-history|title=50 Best Defensive Midfielders in World Football History|first=Michael|last=Cummings|website=Bleacherreport.com|access-date=9 July 2026}}</ref>

A [[Midfielder#Defensive midfielder|defensive midfielder]] with the ability to contribute offensively and [[Playmaker|creatively]], he turned professional playing for [[Argentinos Juniors]] and played one full decade in [[La Liga]], for [[CD Tenerife|Tenerife]] and [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]], then finished his career (curtailed by several injury problems) in Italy, with [[AC Milan]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fantagazzetta.com/approfondimenti/il-regista-di-centrocampo-da-redondo-a-verratti-passando-per-pirlo-e-xavi-169591|title=Il regista di centrocampo: da Redondo a Verratti passando per Pirlo e Xavi|trans-title=Midfield playmakers: from Redondo to Verratti through Pirlo and Xavi|publisher=Fanta Gazzetta|language=it|date=31 March 2013|access-date=3 December 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.magliarossonera.it/protagonisti/Gioc-Redondo.html|title=Fernando Carlos Redondo Neri "Il Principe"|trans-title=Fernando Carlos Redondo Neri "The Prince"|publisher=Maglia Rossonera|language=it|access-date=3 December 2014}}</ref> With Real Madrid, he won two [[La Liga]] championships and as many [[UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] trophies, adding the [[2003 UEFA Champions League final|2003 Champions League]] with Milan.

Redondo was a member of the [[Argentina national football team|Argentina national team]] in the 1990s, representing the nation in the [[1994 FIFA World Cup|1994 World Cup]], and also winning the [[1992 King Fahd Cup|1992 FIFA Confederations Cup]] and the [[1993 Copa América]].

==Club career==
===Early years / Tenerife===
Born in [[Adrogué]], [[Buenos Aires Province]], Redondo played his first game in the [[Argentine Primera División|Primera División]] at only 16 for [[Argentinos Juniors]], and remained five years with the team before moving abroad to Spain.

Redondo made his debut in [[La Liga]] with [[CD Tenerife|Tenerife]], under the management of countryman [[Jorge Solari]]. During this period, [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] twice lost the league title to arch-rivals [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] on the final day of the season, in matches against Tenerife who were managed by [[Jorge Valdano]]<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.marca.com/en/football/real-madrid/2017/07/10/596381e8468aeb567d8b45e5.html|title=Fernando Redondo: The man with magnets in his boots who stole two titles from Real Madrid|newspaper=[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]]|first1=Joel|last1=Del Río|first2=Padraig|last2=Whelan|date=10 July 2017|access-date=23 December 2017}}</ref> and, when the coach was appointed at Real Madrid in the summer of 1994, the player also made the move for a fee of [[United States dollar|US$]]5 million.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://elpais.com/diario/1994/04/20/deportes/766792803_850215.html|title=Acuerdo entre el Madrid y el Tenerife para el traspaso de Redondo|trans-title=Acuerdo between Madrid and Tenerife for transfer of Redondo|newspaper=[[El País]]|first1=Mábel|last1=Galaz|first2=Santiago|last2=Segurola|language=es|date=20 April 1994|access-date=3 September 2018}}</ref>

===Real Madrid===
The key years of Redondo's career were spent at Real Madrid, where he won two league championships and the [[UEFA Champions League]] in [[1997–98 UEFA Champions League|1998]] and [[1999–2000 UEFA Champions League|2000]]. During the second victorious campaign in the latter competition, his performances won him the competition's [[UEFA Champions League Most Valuable Player#Most Valuable Player|Most Valuable Player]] award, with new coach [[Vicente del Bosque]] utilising him in a midfield combination with [[Steve McManaman]]. In the quarter-finals against [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] at [[Old Trafford]], he was the author of a spectacular play in which he [[dribble]]d past [[Henning Berg]] by backheeling the ball around him, recovering it and assisting [[Raúl (footballer)|Raúl]] for his side's third goal (3–2 win, 3–2 on aggregate); after the game, opposing manager [[Alex Ferguson]] said: "What does this player have in his boots? A magnet?”<ref name=Touch>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2000/may/21/newsstory.sport1|title=One-touch perfectionist|newspaper=[[The Guardian]]|first=Simon|last=Kuper|date=21 May 2000|access-date=18 January 2010}}</ref> For his performances, he was subsequently voted the Champions League and [[UEFA Club Footballer of the Year]].<ref name=POTY>{{cite web|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/886544.stm|title=Euro coaches name Redondo the best|work=[[BBC Sport]]|date=18 August 2000|access-date=23 December 2017}}</ref>

During his time in Madrid, Redondo earned the nickname ''El Principe'' ("The Prince").<ref name=Prince>{{cite news|url=http://www.nysun.com/sports/prince-retires/5566/|title=A prince retires|newspaper=[[The New York Sun]]|first=Paul|last=Gardner|date=30 November 2004|access-date=29 July 2013}}</ref> In April 2013, he was named by daily newspaper [[Marca (newspaper)|''Marca'']] as a member of the "Best foreign eleven in [[History of Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid's history]]"<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.marca.com/2013/04/11/en/football/real_madrid/1365709938.html|title=The best foreign eleven in Real Madrid's history|newspaper=Marca|date=11 April 2013|access-date=12 April 2013}}</ref> and, four years later, was selected by its readers to be part of the club's all-time XI;<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.marca.com/en/football/real-madrid/2017/12/22/5a3cd3b2e2704e9a598b45a5.html|title=Readers pick their all-time Real Madrid XI|newspaper=Marca|first=Sergio|last=García|date=22 December 2017|access-date=23 December 2017}}</ref> during one full decade, he amassed Spanish top division totals of 268 games and 12 goals.

===AC Milan===
In 2000, Redondo transferred to [[Serie A]] club [[A.C. Milan]] in a controversial [[Pound sterling|£]]11m move: he stated that he was not involved in transfer discussions and expressed his desire to stay at Madrid.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2000/jul/28/newsstory.sport6|title=Furious Redondo joins Milan for £11m|newspaper=The Guardian|date=28 July 2000|access-date=28 July 2013}}</ref> In response, a section of Real Madrid supporters gathered outside the [[Santiago Bernabéu Stadium|Santiago Bernabéu]] protesting the transfer.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/europe/854961.stm|title=Madrid lose Redondo to Milan|work=BBC Sport|date=27 July 2000|access-date=28 July 2013}}</ref> However, he suffered a serious knee injury in one of his first training sessions for his new team, and was unable to play for the next {{frac|2|1|2}} years; he suspended his £2.74m-a-year salary, and even tried to give back the house and car which the Milan board had given him.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2008/feb/13/theknowledge.sport|title=Football knowledge: Players who fell short of a century of caps|newspaper=The Guardian|first1=Richard|last1=Aikman|first2=Barney|last2=Ronay|first3=Nicky|last3=Bandini|date=13 February 2008|access-date=24 May 2008}}</ref>

Redondo did manage to contribute (albeit in a peripheral role) to Milan's successes in the [[2002–03 A.C. Milan season|2002–03]] and [[2003–04 A.C. Milan season|2003–04 seasons]], making a combined 16 league appearances and adding five in the [[2002–03 UEFA Champions League|2002–03 Champions League]] and six in [[2002–03 Coppa Italia|the same edition]] of the [[Coppa Italia]], including the [[2003 Coppa Italia Final|two-legged final]].<ref>Almanacco illustrato del Milan, 2ª ed., Panini, Marzo 2005, p. 612</ref> In late 2004, at the age of 35, he retired from professional football following another knee injury.<ref name=Prince/>

==International career==
Redondo earned 29 [[Cap (sport)|caps]] for [[Argentina national football team|Argentina]], the bulk of his appearances coming from 1992 to 1994 while [[Alfio Basile]] was the manager. His first appearance was on 18 June 1992, in a 2–0 [[Exhibition game|friendly]] win over [[Australia men's national soccer team|Australia]].

Redondo turned down a call-up to the national team just before the [[1990 FIFA World Cup]], when it was coached by [[Carlos Salvador Bilardo]]. The player excused himself on account of not wanting to interrupt his law studies, but it was also reported that he objected to Bilardo's defensive strategy.<ref name=Touch/><ref name=Prince/> Redondo later explained: "I was picked for Argentina's World Cup squad in 1990 but I knew I wasn't going to be in the starting line-up, I would just be another squad member, so I preferred to stay home."<ref name=Free>{{cite web|url=http://www.thefreelibrary.com/Football:+RED+ALERT;+Two-year+agony+over+as+Milan+ace+roars+back.-a096371653|title=Two-year agony over as Milan ace roars back|publisher=The Free Library|first=Keir|last=Radnedge|date=13 January 2003|access-date=8 November 2010}}</ref>

In the [[1994 FIFA World Cup|1994 World Cup]], Redondo started in all of Argentina's matches, but was unable to prevent the country from falling 2–3 to [[Romania national football team|Romania]] in the [[Single-elimination tournament|round of 16]]. Following the tournament in the United States, he refused to play under [[Daniel Passarella]], who had banned long hair, earrings and homosexuals in his squad, leading to disputes with several players.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/world_cup_98/teams/argentina/players/85306.stm|title=Daniel Passarella – Argentinian manager|publisher=[[BBC]]|date=2 May 1998|access-date=28 July 2013}}</ref> The former refused the latter's demand to cut his hair, and was left out of the national team as even [[Diego Maradona]] and president [[Carlos Menem]] went on to take sides in the situation.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.itnsource.com/shotlist//RTV/1995/09/06/605230241/?s=criticises|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140513095325/http://www.itnsource.com/shotlist//RTV/1995/09/06/605230241/?s=criticises|url-status=dead|archive-date=13 May 2014|title=Spain/Argentina: Argentina's major controversy of the moment-the length of midfielder Fernando Redondo's hair|publisher=[[ITN#ITN Source|ITN Source]]|date=6 September 1995|access-date=29 July 2013}}</ref>

Passarella excluded Redondo from his [[1998 FIFA World Cup|1998 World Cup]] squad, stating: "Twice he was asked to play for the national team and twice he refused and gave a different reason each time. Then he announced publicly he did not want to play for the national team and I do not pick any player who does not want to play for Argentina."<ref>{{cite news|url=http://archives.tcm.ie/irishexaminer/1998/04/22/phead.htm|title=Ace Batistuta keen to play for Liverpool|newspaper=[[Irish Examiner]]|first=Bill|last=George|date=22 April 1998|access-date=2 May 2010|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110629114324/http://archives.tcm.ie/irishexaminer/1998/04/22/phead.htm|archive-date=29 June 2011}}</ref> The player later explained: "I was in great form. But he had particular ideas about discipline and wanted me to have my hair cut. I didn't see what that had to do with playing football so I said no again."<ref name=Free/>

In 1999, when Argentina was managed by [[Marcelo Bielsa]], Redondo was recalled to the national side for two exhibition matches with [[Brazil national football team|Brazil]]. Although he was chosen ''[[Player of the match]]'' in the 2–0 victory in [[Buenos Aires]] he refused any subsequent call-ups, preferring to focus on club football; in 2015, he was included in an all-time team by the [[Argentine Football Association]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/soccer/news/best-ever-argentina-starting-lineup-includes-messi-and-maradona/|title=Best ever Argentina starting lineup includes Messi and Maradona|work=[[CBS Sports]]|first=Roger|last=Gonzalez|date=4 January 2016|access-date=23 December 2017}}</ref>

==Style of play==
An elegant [[Playmaker#Deep-lying playmakers|deep-lying playmaker]] who played in front of the defence,<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/these-football-times/2015/apr/24/age-position-football-michael-carrick-andrea-pirlo-xabi-alonso|title=The relationship between a player's age and their position on a football pitch|newspaper=The Guardian|first=Blair|last=Newman|date=24 April 2015|access-date=24 September 2015}}</ref> Redondo's main attributes were his creative passing, vision, technique and close control with his left foot, his ability to control the tempo of his team's play in midfield making him a key member of the Real Madrid side of the 90s.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/sport/football/champions_league/759401.stm|title=Real Madrid's key players|work=BBC Sport|date=23 May 2000|access-date=24 September 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fourfourtwo.com/features/ivan-zamorano-perfect-xi#:ziECP2LWWdLipA|title=Ivan Zamorano: Perfect XI|publisher=[[FourFourTwo]]|date=1 August 2010|access-date=24 September 2015}}</ref><ref name=Prince2>{{cite web|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/en/about-real-madrid/history/football-legends/fernando-carlos-redondo-neri|title=A prince at the Bernabéu|publisher=Real Madrid CF|access-date=24 September 2015}}</ref> Despite not having a great deal of pace, he possessed good acceleration and was an efficient and aggressive tackler, who contributed defensively just as much as he did offensively.<ref name=Sentinel>{{cite news|url=https://www.orlandosentinel.com/1994/06/15/baggio-takes-great-strides-toward-soccer-greatness/|title=Baggio takes great strides toward soccer greatness|newspaper=[[Orlando Sentinel]]|first=Mike|last=Zizzo|date=15 June 1994|access-date=24 September 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.centrocampista.com/2012/02/fernando-redondo/|title=When El Rey Fernando ruled Madrid|publisher=El Centrocampista|first=Sam|last=Hughes|date=11 February 2012|access-date=16 May 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.managingmadrid.com/2017/5/9/15498724/fernando-redondo-the-pure-essence-of-elegance|title=Fernando Redondo: The pure essence of elegance|publisher=[[SB Nation]]|first=Paul|last=Ondra|date=9 May 2017|access-date=23 December 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.acmilan.com/en/news/tbt/2017-02-02/tbt-redondo-a-lord-of-football|title=Redondo, a lord of football|publisher=A.C. Milan|date=6 June 2017|access-date=23 December 2017}}</ref> As such, his role has also been likened to that of a ''[[Midfielder#Centre-half|metodista]]'' ("centre-half," in Italian football jargon), due to his ability to dictate play in midfield as well as assist his team defensively.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.rivistaundici.com/2017/02/24/cinque-nuovo-dieci/ |title=Il 5 è il nuovo 10 |trans-title=The 5 is the new 10 |publisher=Rivista Undici |language=it-IT |last1=Carriero |first1=Cristiano |last2=Tossani |first2=Michele |date=24 February 2017 |access-date=15 February 2024 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.ultimouomo.com/che-fine-hanno-fatto-i-nostri-preferiti/ |title=Che fine hanno fatto i nostri "Preferiti" |publisher=L'Ultimo Uomo |language=it-IT |date=19 October 2023 |access-date=15 February 2024 }}</ref><ref name="taconazo"/> [[Fabio Capello]] described Redondo as "tactically perfect".<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2000/may/21/newsstory.sport1|title=One-touch perfectionist|date=21 May 2000|access-date=9 July 2026|newspaper=[[The Guardian]]}}</ref>

Although he was regarded as one of the greatest midfielders of his generation,<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1998/06/30/sports/world-cup-98-argentina-s-coach-knows-way-to-ultimate-prize.html|title=World Cup '98; Argentina's coach knows way to ultimate prize|newspaper=[[The New York Times]]|first=Christopher|last=Clarey|date=30 June 1998|access-date=24 September 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1998-jun-13-sp-59584-story.html|title=For a world of reasons, many standouts are sitting this out|newspaper=[[Los Angeles Times]]|first=Mike|last=Penner|date=13 June 1998|access-date=24 September 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.skysports.com/football/news/11672/2296656/spurs-keep-tabs-on-redondo|title=Spurs keep tabs on Redondo|publisher=[[Sky Sports]]|first=Nadia|last=Carminati|access-date=24 September 2015}}</ref> Redondo's career was also largely marked by injuries, in particular during the final years of his career.<ref name=Sentinel/><ref name=Prince2/>

==Personal life==
Redondo was born into an industrialist family and enjoyed a wealthy upbringing, later studying law at university in the early years of his playing career.<ref name="taconazo">{{cite news|url=http://milano.corriere.it/notizie/cronaca/13_novembre_12/redondo-el-taconazo-che-leggeva-borges-375b3e3c-4b77-11e3-9f20-48230e8bb565.shtml|title=Redondo, "el taconazo" che leggeva Borges|trans-title=Redondo, "el taconazo" who read Borges|newspaper=[[Corriere della Sera]]|first=Roberto|last=Perrone|language=it|date=14 November 2013|access-date=7 November 2016}}</ref> He married the cousin of fellow footballer [[Santiago Solari]],<ref>{{cite news|url=http://old.ole.com.ar/diario/1999/10/30/r-02601e.htm|title=Que hoy nos dejen muy bien parados|trans-title=May our name be held very high today|newspaper=[[Olé (sports newspaper)|Olé]]|first=Enrique|last=Romero|language=es|date=30 October 1999|access-date=7 November 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161107220845/http://old.ole.com.ar/diario/1999/10/30/r-02601e.htm|archive-date=7 November 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> and his sons [[Federico Redondo|Federico]] and [[Fernando Redondo (footballer, born 1994)|Fernando Jr.]] were also involved in the sport.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://as.com/futbol/2016/02/05/internacional/1454711491_012934.html|title=El hijo de Fernando Redondo debuta mañana en Tigre|trans-title=Son of Fernando Redondo makes debut with Tigre tomorrow|newspaper=[[Diario AS]]|first=Verónica|last=Brunati|language=es|date=5 February 2016|access-date=2 November 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.minutouno.com/notas/3041617-federico-redondo-hijo-fernando-comienza-entrenar-la-seleccion-sub-15|title=Federico Redondo, hijo de Fernando, comienza a entrenar con la Selección Sub 15|trans-title=Federico Redondo, son of Fernando, starts training with the Under-15 national team|publisher=Minuto Uno|language=es|date=24 September 2017|access-date=2 November 2017}}</ref>

An avid reader, Redondo counted [[Jorge Luis Borges]] and [[Gabriel García Márquez]] as his two favourite authors.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://ricerca.repubblica.it/repubblica/archivio/repubblica/2002/01/10/il-mistero-redondo-alla-prova-del-campo.html|title=Il mistero Redondo alla prova del campo – Rientro nel Milan dopo due anni di stop|trans-title=The Redondo mystery tests the pitch – Return to Milan after two years of inactivity|newspaper=[[La Repubblica]]|first=Luigi|last=Bolognini|language=it|date=10 January 2002|access-date=7 November 2016}}</ref>
